name: Ways of working
description: Therapeutic approaches and methods a practitioner uses. Each has a short label for chips, a full name and a plain-language description for clients. Practitioners pick as many as apply, and can mark any of them as 'in training'.

categories.label: Mind & body
categories.hint: Through the body, breath and attention

items.name: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)
items.description: Looks at how thoughts, feelings and actions feed into each other, and builds practical skills to change patterns that keep you stuck.

items.name: Dialectical behaviour therapy (DBT)
items.description: Skills for riding out intense emotions, handling distress and keeping relationships steady.

items.name: Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT)
items.description: Helps you make room for difficult thoughts and feelings while moving towards what matters to you.

items.name: Rational emotive behaviour therapy (REBT)
items.description: Challenges rigid 'musts' and 'shoulds' that drive upsetting feelings, and replaces them with more flexible beliefs.

items.name: Schema therapy
items.description: Works on deep-rooted patterns formed early in life, such as feeling unlovable or expecting to be abandoned, and how they play out now.

items.name: Compassion-focused therapy (CFT)
items.description: Helps quieten harsh self-criticism and shame by building a kinder, steadier inner voice.

items.name: Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT)
items.description: Combines mindfulness practice with CBT tools, often used to stop depression from coming back.

items.name: Behaviour therapy
items.description: Changes habits and responses step by step, with clear goals and practice between sessions.

items.name: Exposure and response prevention (ERP)
items.description: The main therapy for OCD and phobias: facing fears a step at a time while resisting the urge to check, avoid or seek reassurance.

items.name: Psychodynamic therapy
items.description: Explores how earlier experiences and less visible patterns shape how you feel and relate today.

items.name: Person-centred therapy
items.description: A warm, non-judgemental space where you set the pace and the therapist follows your lead.

items.name: Supportive counselling
items.description: A steady space to talk things through, feel heard and find your footing again.

items.name: Gestalt therapy
items.description: Focuses on what you are feeling and doing right now, in the session, to bring hidden patterns into awareness.

items.name: Existential therapy
items.description: Makes room for big questions about meaning, choice, loss and purpose.

items.name: Transactional analysis (TA)
items.description: Looks at the 'parent', 'adult' and 'child' sides of how you relate, and the patterns that keep repeating with people.

items.name: Interpersonal therapy (IPT)
items.description: Short-term work on the relationships, conflicts and role changes linked to low mood.

items.name: Emotion-focused therapy (EFT)
items.description: Helps you notice, understand and work with your emotions, rather than push them away.

items.name: Narrative therapy
items.description: Helps you step back from the stories you tell about yourself and rewrite the ones that hold you back.

items.name: Solution-focused brief therapy (SFBT)
items.description: Short-term, goal-focused work that builds on what is already working in your life.

items.name: Positive psychology
items.description: Builds on your strengths, values and what gives you energy, alongside working on what's hard.

items.name: EMDR
items.description: A structured therapy that helps the mind process distressing or traumatic memories.

items.name: Trauma-focused CBT (TF-CBT)
items.description: A structured CBT programme for children, teens and their caregivers after a traumatic experience.

items.name: Internal family systems (IFS)
items.description: Works with the different 'parts' of you with curiosity, so they can stop pulling against each other.

items.name: Trauma-informed practice
items.description: Not a single method but a way of working that puts safety, choice and pacing first for anyone who has been through trauma.

items.name: Couples counselling
items.description: Sessions for partners together, to talk through problems, communicate better and decide on next steps.

items.name: Premarital counselling
items.description: Helps couples talk through expectations, families, money and conflict before marriage.

items.name: Gottman method couples therapy
items.description: Research-based couples work on communication, conflict and friendship, with practical exercises to try at home.

items.name: Emotionally focused couples therapy (EFT)
items.description: Helps partners understand the emotional cycle behind their arguments and rebuild a secure bond.

items.name: Family systems therapy
items.description: Works with the family as a whole, looking at roles, patterns and communication between members.

items.name: Parent–child interaction therapy (PCIT)
items.description: Coaches parents live while they play with their child, to improve behaviour and strengthen the bond.

items.name: Parent coaching and training
items.description: Practical guidance for parents on routines, behaviour, communication and staying calm.

items.name: Art therapy
items.description: Uses drawing, painting and making to express what is hard to put into words.

items.name: Expressive arts
items.description: Brings together art, movement, writing and play as ways to explore feelings.

items.name: Drama therapy
items.description: Uses role-play, story and enactment to look at experiences from a safe distance.

items.name: Psychodrama
items.description: Acts out real situations from your life, often in a group, to see them freshly and try new responses.

items.name: Play therapy
items.description: Uses play as a language for working through feelings, especially with younger clients.

items.name: Sand tray therapy
items.description: Uses miniature figures in a tray of sand to build scenes that show what's going on inside.

items.name: Music therapy
items.description: Uses listening, rhythm and making music to reach feelings that are hard to talk about.

items.name: Dance and movement therapy
items.description: Uses movement and the body as a way into emotions and memories.

items.name: Therapeutic writing and journaling
items.description: Uses guided writing and journaling to process experiences and notice patterns between sessions.

items.name: Mindfulness-based therapy
items.description: Builds the habit of noticing thoughts and feelings without getting swept up in them.

items.name: Somatic therapy
items.description: Pays attention to how stress and emotion show up in the body.

items.name: Hypnotherapy
items.description: Uses guided, focused relaxation to work with stress, anxiety and habits.

items.name: Relaxation and breathwork
items.description: Breathing, muscle relaxation and grounding techniques to calm the nervous system.

items.name: Yoga-informed therapy
items.description: Brings gentle movement, breath and body awareness from yoga into therapy.

items.name: Sound therapy
items.description: Uses sound, vibration and listening to relax the body and settle the mind.

items.name: Career counselling
items.description: Guidance on study and career choices, transitions and direction at work.

items.name: Philosophical counselling
items.description: Thinks through life questions and values with the help of philosophical ideas.

items.name: Psychoeducation
items.description: Clear explanations of what you're going through and how it works, so you and your family can manage it with confidence.

items.name: Motivational interviewing (MI)
items.description: A collaborative conversation that helps you find your own reasons to change, often used with habits and substance use.

items.name: Psychological assessment
items.description: Standardised tests and interviews to understand things like learning, attention, autism or personality, with a written report.

items.name: Eclectic approach
items.description: Draws on different methods and shapes the work around what you need.
